questions.question: What makes chromatography highly versatile when dealing with extremely tiny quantities of a mixture?
options: It can only be used on solid mixtures.
It can be used for both the separation of minute samples and analysis.
It requires the substances to have identical boiling points.
It converts all components into gases instantly.

questions.question: If a scientist runs a paper chromatography test on a sample and observes only a single spot on the finished chromatogram, what does this indicate about the sample?
options: The sample is a mixture of many different liquids.
The sample is a pure substance.
The solvent failed to move up the paper.
The sample has reacted with the pencil line.

questions.question: How does the chromatogram of a mixture differ from that of a pure substance?
options: A mixture will produce many spots on a chromatogram.
A mixture will only produce one spot at the very top.
A mixture will prevent the solvent from rising.
A mixture dissolves the chromatography paper.

questions.question: How can a forensic scientist identify an unknown ink dye from a crime scene using chromatography?
options: By measuring the exact weight of the paper before and after.
By burning the chromatogram to see the flame color.
By comparing its chromatogram with chromatograms of known ink samples.
By mixing the unknown ink with a liquid of the same density.

questions.question: Why is a pencil, rather than a pen, used to draw the baseline on chromatography paper?
options: Pencil lead reacts chemically with all solvents.
Pencil is insoluble in water, so it won't run and interfere with the results.
Pencil marks are magnetic and assist the separation.
Pencil marks automatically guide the solvent up the paper in a straight line.

questions.question: Under what conditions is fractional distillation preferred over simple distillation?
options: When separating a mixture with three or more substances, or substances with similar boiling points.
When separating an insoluble solid from a highly viscous liquid.
When the substances in the mixture have identical densities.
When one of the substances is magnetic and the other is not.

questions.question: What is the consequence if the condenser in a distillation setup begins to warm up during the process?
options: The distillation process will speed up significantly.
The condenser becomes less effective, and more gas will escape without condensing.
The distillate will immediately turn back into a solid.
It prevents the mixture in the flask from boiling.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the process of crystallisation?
options: It is the rapid boiling of a solvent until only a dry powder remains.
It reforms a solute as crystals from a saturated solution following a change in conditions.
It uses a magnetic field to align molecules into rigid structures.
It separates two miscible liquids by their differing densities.

questions.question: If you want to obtain larger, well-defined crystals during crystallisation, how should the solvent be allowed to evaporate?
options: It should be evaporated as quickly as possible by boiling.
It should be evaporated more slowly.
It should not be allowed to evaporate at all.
It should be evaporated using a high-pressure vacuum.

questions.question: Which materials are attracted to magnets, making magnetic separation a viable method to remove them from a mixture?
options: Copper and aluminium
Iron and steel
Zinc and brass
Gold and silver

questions.question: What process is used to separate insoluble solids from a liquid by passing the mixture through a barrier?
options: Distillation
Chromatography
Filtration
Crystallisation

questions.question: What is a key characteristic of immiscible liquids when they are mixed and then allowed to settle?
options: They chemically react to form a solid precipitate.
They do not mix, and one liquid will float above the other.
They completely dissolve into one another to form a single phase.
They instantly evaporate into the surrounding air.

questions.question: Which techniques are most suitable for separating a mixture of two immiscible liquids like oil and water?
options: Simple distillation or fractional distillation
Decanting or using a separating funnel
Paper chromatography or filtration
Evaporation or crystallisation

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of techniques required to separate pure salt from a sample of rock salt?
options: Simple distillation, chromatography, and decanting
Making a solution, filtration, and crystallisation
Fractional distillation, magnetic separation, and evaporation
Centrifuging, chromatography, and condensation

questions.question: Why is it important to keep the condenser cold during a distillation experiment?
options: To prevent the flask from overheating and exploding.
To speed up the condensation of the vaporised liquid.
To ensure the solute does not precipitate inside the tube.
To keep the boiling point of the mixture low.
